episode.title: Preserve literal file paths containing glob metacharacters across workspace-rooted file tools
episode.before: At parent commit fb3ceb0da4e2cd636013c2c36a9c0016c01aa47f, both file-discovery operations passed user inputs directly to the glob library after only separator normalization in the multi-file reader. Consequently, an existing workspace-relative path containing glob metacharacters such as square brackets was interpreted as a pattern rather than as the literal path, so exact files such as file[1].txt or src/app/[test]/(dashboard)/testing/components/code.tsx could be missed.
episode.after: At commit 6fc68ff8d4536f35f0ed76af535d5e1e7ac37675, each operation resolves an input against every applicable workspace search directory, checks whether that exact path exists, and escapes the input before glob evaluation when it does. Nonexistent inputs remain unescaped and therefore retain wildcard-pattern behavior. Focused tests cover literal bracketed filenames and nested paths containing square brackets and parentheses for both discovery and multi-file reading.
episode.diff: The change imports filesystem existence checks and the glob library's escape helper. The discovery operation now classifies its single input independently for each search directory and escapes an existing literal path. The multi-file reader similarly normalizes and classifies every search input independently for each workspace root, passing escaped existing paths and unchanged nonexisting patterns to glob. Four regression tests were added: two for discovery and two for reading. Existing workspace selection, ignore filtering, containment checks, result formatting, and wildcard behavior were left in place.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 6fc68ff8d4536f35f0ed76af535d5e1e7ac37675 has parent fb3ceb0da4e2cd636013c2c36a9c0016c01aa47f, is titled "fix(tools): Handle special characters in file paths for glob and read_many_files (#6507)", and changes two implementations plus their two test files.

Before the change, the discovery operation called glob(this.params.pattern, { cwd: searchDir, ... }) directly for every workspace search directory, with no exact-path existence check or escaping step.

After the change, the discovery operation joins each search directory with the supplied input, checks fs.existsSync(fullPath), escapes the input when the exact path exists, and then evaluates the resulting value with cwd set to that search directory.

Before the change, the multi-file reader normalized backslashes in all search inputs and passed the resulting array directly to glob for each workspace directory; it did not distinguish existing literal paths from patterns.

After the change, the multi-file reader processes every input separately under every workspace directory: it normalizes separators, joins the input to the current directory, escapes it if that exact path exists, otherwise preserves it as a glob pattern, and then evaluates the processed array.

The implementation diff adds fs/existsSync and glob escape usage, replacing direct glob submission with existence-gated escaping while retaining the surrounding workspace iteration and filtering pipeline.

Discovery regression tests create file[1].txt and a nested src/app/[test]/(dashboard)/testing/components/code.tsx file, invoke the tool with each exact relative path, and require one result containing the literal created path.

Multi-file-reader regression tests create the same two forms of special-character paths, request each exact relative path, and require the returned content and success display to identify exactly one file.

The discovery test suite retains tests using wildcard inputs such as *.TXT, sub/*.md, and **/*.log, establishing that wildcard interpretation remains part of the required contract alongside the new literal-path behavior.
The changed discovery and multi-file reader classes are registered as core tools, and the core prompt directs the agent to use them for repository discovery and contextual reading.

candidate_atomics.name: escape-existing-literal-before-pattern-discovery
candidate_atomics.title: Protect an existing literal path before pattern-based discovery
candidate_atomics.description: For each applicable search root, distinguish an existing exact path from a pattern and escape the exact path before sending it to the pattern engine, while leaving nonexistent inputs available for wildcard matching.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a file-discovery interface that accepts both exact paths and wildcard patterns to locate existing names containing pattern metacharacters without disabling wildcard searches.
semantic_action.pre_state: A user-supplied relative input is about to be evaluated by a pattern engine under one or more workspace search roots, and an existing literal path may contain characters meaningful to that engine.
semantic_action.post_state: Under each search root, an input resolving to an existing exact path is escaped and treated literally; an input not resolving to an exact path remains a pattern.
semantic_action.validation: Create exact files whose names and directory segments contain square brackets or parentheses, request their literal relative paths, and require one discovery result containing each exact path; retain wildcard tests to ensure patterns still expand.

candidate_atomics.name: escape-existing-literals-before-batch-read-expansion
candidate_atomics.title: Protect existing literal paths before batch-read expansion
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize and classify every batch-read input independently against each workspace root, escaping exact existing paths while preserving inputs that should remain patterns.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure a batch file-reading interface can read exact files with pattern metacharacters while continuing to support wildcard inputs and multiple workspace roots.
semantic_action.pre_state: A batch-reading request contains path-or-pattern inputs that will be expanded by a pattern engine for each workspace root; literal inputs may contain metacharacters and platform-specific separators.
semantic_action.post_state: Each input is separator-normalized and evaluated relative to each workspace root; an existing exact path is escaped before expansion, while a nonexisting input remains an unescaped pattern.
semantic_action.validation: Create files with bracketed names and nested bracket/parenthesis path segments, request each as an exact input, and require the reader to return the exact file content and report one successfully read file.

candidate_workflows.name: resolve-literal-paths-at-workspace-rooted-pattern-boundaries
candidate_workflows.title: Preserve exact special-character paths across workspace-rooted file operations
candidate_workflows.description: Apply one literal-versus-pattern rule at each file-operation boundary that delegates to a glob engine: resolve the input under the actual search root, escape it only when that exact path exists, and validate both exact-path and wildcard behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: Exact workspace-relative paths containing glob metacharacters are discovered and read literally, while genuine wildcard inputs continue to expand under every intended workspace root.
when_to_use: A file interface accepts both exact relative paths and glob-style patterns through the same parameter.
Existing files or directories contain characters such as square brackets or parentheses that the delegated pattern engine may interpret specially.
The operation evaluates inputs relative to one or more configured workspace or worktree roots.
anti_goals: Do not globally escape every input, because doing so would disable intentional wildcard expansion.
Do not change workspace containment, ignore filtering, sorting, content formatting, or file-processing behavior unrelated to input interpretation.
Do not probe only the process current directory or one global target root when pattern evaluation occurs under multiple workspace roots.
not_applicable_when: The interface has separate, unambiguous parameters for literal paths and patterns and never sends literal paths through a pattern engine.
The downstream selector already guarantees literal treatment for exact-path inputs containing metacharacters.
No reliable search root is available for resolving whether an input denotes an existing exact path.
inputs: configured workspace or worktree search roots
workflow_graph.entry_state: One or more workspace-rooted file operations pass ambiguous path-or-pattern inputs directly to a pattern engine, causing existing special-character paths to be interpreted as patterns.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every affected operation resolves and classifies inputs under the same root used by its pattern engine, protects exact existing paths with escaping, preserves nonexisting inputs as patterns, and has focused regression coverage for literal metacharacters plus retained wildcard coverage.

steps.condition: The affected discovery operation accepts a single path-or-pattern input and evaluates it independently under workspace search roots.
steps.validation: Literal bracketed filenames and nested special-character paths each produce one exact discovery result, while wildcard discovery tests remain satisfied.

steps.condition: A batch-reading operation independently accepts path-or-pattern inputs and expands them under every workspace root.
steps.validation: Each literal special-character input returns the exact created file content and reports one successfully read file.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent implementation to confirm ambiguous inputs are passed directly to the pattern engine.
Verify the implementation checks exact-path existence relative to the current search root before escaping.
Run focused discovery tests for a bracketed filename and a nested path containing brackets and parentheses.
Run focused batch-reader tests for the same literal-path forms and verify exact content.
Run retained wildcard-pattern tests and the broader affected package suite to detect accidental loss of pattern, filtering, or workspace behavior.
stop_conditions: Stop if the candidate path is resolved against a different root from the pattern engine's cwd; the classification would be unreliable.
Stop if all inputs must be escaped to pass the regression, because that breaks the mixed literal-and-pattern contract.
Stop if focused exact-path tests pass but existing wildcard tests fail.
Defer completion if the affected package tests cannot be executed and no external successful validation result is available.

GitHub PR body, reviews, discussion, and status checks were unavailable, so design rationale beyond the implementation and tests is deferred.
The implementation treats any existing filesystem path as literal before glob evaluation; behavior for an intentionally glob-like input that also names an existing path is not explicitly tested.

unresolved_questions: Did CI or maintainer review validate the complete core package suite for commit 6fc68ff8d4536f35f0ed76af535d5e1e7ac37675? The supplied GitHub bundle contains no status checks or reviews.

Should an input that is intentionally a glob but also exactly matches an existing metacharacter-containing path be treated as literal or as a pattern? The implementation chooses literal, but no explicit ambiguity test or discussion was available.
The supplied routing class emphasizes root/worktree resolution; the directly evidenced defect is more specifically literal-versus-pattern disambiguation performed relative to each workspace root.
